root.label: Judge orders DOJ memo on boat strikes submitted for confidential review

events.label: Judge orders DOJ memo on boat strikes submitted for confidential review

slots.name: opinion page count
slots.sentence: U.S. District Judge Paul Engelmayer rejected two of the administration’s three arguments to keep the document secret in a 66-page opinion, requiring that the government submit the memo within two weeks for his confidential review.

slots.name: legal organization count
slots.sentence: Three legal organizations — the American Civil Liberties Union, the New York Civil Liberties Union and the Center for Constitutional Rights — filed a Freedom of Information Act lawsuit last year to demand the release of this memo and other records related to these strikes.

slots.name: memo page count
slots.sentence: The memo from the DOJ’s Office of Legal Counsel is reportedly more than 40 pages long, according to The New York Times, and addressed the legal standards justifying these strikes.

slots.name: memo submission deadline
slots.sentence: requiring that the government submit the memo within two weeks for his confidential review.

slots.name: ruling status
slots.sentence: Engelmayer’s ruling does not necessarily mean that the entire DOJ memo will be made public.
